findings.title: Disposal-only live-handle behavior is not discriminated

rejecting_example.candidate: Correct ordinary close; asyncDispose resolves without teardown.
specified_trace: Close writer ordinarily; accepted prefix becomes durable and ownership releases.
Repeat close and invoke asyncDispose on already closed writer.
Verify typed-closed operations and no leaks.
rejecting_example.why_it_can_pass: Ordinary close has already established every observed teardown condition; no-op disposal on the closed handle preserves them.
rejecting_example.missing_trace: Fresh active writer -> append -> asyncDispose only -> await -> independent durability and ownership checks; fresh reader disposal too.

findings.title: No changed-log transition discriminates an unsound constant revision

rejecting_example.candidate: Correct current read/stat/list data; one constant revision per service instance/session.
specified_trace: Observe metadata and compare same-instance/session revisions.
Exercise ownership-only churn; revision remains constant.
rejecting_example.why_it_can_pass: No specified SD13 step changes the body between revision observations; SD09 freshness does not compare unchanged tokens against changed bodies.
rejecting_example.missing_trace: Capture body and stat/list revisions -> append nonempty continuation -> resolution barrier -> observe changed body and corresponding revisions -> reject false unchanged-cache eligibility.
